title: Sheet Music
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/904bce6e50f9612f7f82159cbf114937ceb8462e.png) Image generated by ChatGPT 4o.

Alice likes singing. As a singing enthusiast, Alice has listened to countless songs and has tried singing them many times. However, occasionally, some songs make Alice feel bored. After some research, Alice believes that this is because even though the songs she chose are all different, due to her instinctive preference, they all turn out to be musically similar to one another.

To thoroughly analyze this, Alice decided to study the sheet music of the songs. For convenience, Alice represented a song of length $n$ as an integer sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$, where $a_i$ is the pitch of the $i$-th note. Then she defined the musical equivalence between songs. Two songs $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ and $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$ of length $n$ are musically equivalent if for all $1\leq i \lt n$, both $a_i, a_{i+1}$ and $b_{i}, b_{i+1}$ have the same pitch relationship. More specifically, $a_i, a_{i+1}$ and $b_i, b_{i+1}$ have the same pitch relationship if either

- $a_i \lt a_{i + 1}$ and $b_i \lt b_{i + 1}$,
- $a_i = a_{i + 1}$ and $b_i = b_{i + 1}$, or
- $a_i \gt a_{i + 1}$ and $b_i \gt b_{i + 1}$.

For example, $1, 2, 3, 3, 2$ and $5, 9, 13, 13, 1$ are musically equivalent, while $1, 2, 3, 2, 1$ and $1, 2, 2, 2, 1$ are not.

Having practiced consistently for a long time, Alice is able to sing any note in the range of $[1, k]$. She wants to know how many different songs of length $n$ within her range there are, if we treat musically equivalent songs as the same one. Can you help her calculate the number?

Since the answer might be large, print the answer modulo $998244353$.

## Input

The only line contains two integers $n, k$.

- $1\leq n\leq 10^6$
- $1\leq k \leq 10^9$

## Output

Output the number of different songs modulo $998244353$.
statementZhMd:
![图片](https://espresso.codeforces.com/904bce6e50f9612f7f82159cbf114937ceb8462e.png) 图片由 ChatGPT 4o 生成。

Alice 喜欢唱歌。作为一名歌唱爱好者，Alice 听过无数歌曲，也尝试演唱过很多次。然而，偶尔会有一些歌曲让 Alice 感到厌烦。经过一番研究，Alice 认为这是因为，尽管她选择的歌曲各不相同，但由于她本能的偏好，这些歌曲最终在音乐上彼此相似。

为了彻底分析这一现象，Alice 决定研究这些歌曲的乐谱。为方便起见，Alice 将一首长度为 $n$ 的歌曲表示为一个整数序列 $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$，其中 $a_i$ 表示第 $i$ 个音符的音高。随后，她定义了歌曲之间的音乐等价关系。两个长度为 $n$ 的歌曲 $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ 和 $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$ 是音乐等价的，当且仅当对于所有 $1\leq i \lt n$，$a_i, a_{i+1}$ 与 $b_{i}, b_{i+1}$ 的音高关系都相同。更具体地说，$a_i, a_{i+1}$ 与 $b_i, b_{i+1}$ 的音高关系相同，当且仅当以下条件之一成立：

- $a_i \lt a_{i + 1}$ 且 $b_i \lt b_{i + 1}$；
- $a_i = a_{i + 1}$ 且 $b_i = b_{i + 1}$；
- $a_i \gt a_{i + 1}$ 且 $b_i \gt b_{i + 1}$。

例如，$1, 2, 3, 3, 2$ 和 $5, 9, 13, 13, 1$ 是音乐等价的，而 $1, 2, 3, 2, 1$ 和 $1, 2, 2, 2, 1$ 不是。

经过长时间坚持不懈的练习，Alice 已经能够演唱音高在 $[1, k]$ 范围内的任意音符。她想知道，在将音乐等价的歌曲视为同一首歌曲的情况下，长度为 $n$ 且所有音符都在她能力范围内的歌曲共有多少种。请你帮助她计算这个数量。

由于答案可能很大，请将答案对 $998244353$ 取模后输出。

## 输入格式

唯一一行包含两个整数 $n, k$。

- $1\leq n\leq 10^6$
- $1\leq k \leq 10^9$

## 输出格式

输出不同歌曲的数量对 $998244353$ 取模后的结果。
